scheme1_name: CBSE Merit Scholarship Scheme for Single Girl Child (SGC)
scheme2_name: Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY)

comparisons.scheme1_value: Financial aid for meritorious single girl students to continue education in classes 11–12
comparisons.scheme2_value: Low-cost life insurance protection (death cover) for bank account holders

comparisons.scheme1_value: Only single girl children (only child, or all daughters born together) aged 15–17, studying in CBSE class 11–12, with 70%+ in class 10
comparisons.scheme2_value: Any individual aged 18–50 with a bank or post office account

comparisons.scheme1_value: Rs. 1,000 per month for up to 2 years (max Rs. 24,000 total)
comparisons.scheme2_value: Rs. 2 lakh (₹200,000) life insurance cover if you die (any reason)

comparisons.scheme1_value: Free — no fee to apply or receive the scholarship
comparisons.scheme2_value: Rs. 436 per year, auto-debited from your bank account

comparisons.scheme1_value: Family gross income must not exceed Rs. 8 lakh per year
Must study in a CBSE-affiliated school; tuition fee capped at Rs. 2,500/month (class 10) or Rs. 3,000/month (classes 11–12)
comparisons.scheme2_value: No school requirement; banking requirement only

comparisons.scheme1_value: Aadhaar, class 10 mark sheet, school ID, photo, signature, fee receipt, income affidavit (Rs. 50 stamp paper, attested by officer), admission proof
comparisons.scheme2_value: Consent form (downloaded), self-attested KYC (Aadhaar/Voter ID/MGNREGA/Driving Licence), bank account details, nominee info

comparisons.scheme1_value: Online: CBSE scholarship portal (cbse.gov.in/cbsenew/scholar.html); school verification required; print and courier signed confirmation for renewals
comparisons.scheme2_value: Offline: print form, attach KYC, submit to bank/post office. Online: many banks allow enrolment via net banking or mobile banking

comparisons.scheme1_value: Maximum 2 years (classes 11 and 12); renewed annually if marks and conduct maintained
comparisons.scheme2_value: One year (1 June to 31 May); renewable every year as long as premium is paid

comparisons.scheme1_value: Application windows announced yearly on CBSE website — dates vary by session; check current schedule
comparisons.scheme2_value: No fixed deadline; enrol anytime; premium auto-debited every June

comparisons.scheme1_value: Tuition fee caps are strict (over ₹2,500 in class 10 = ineligible). Income must be proven by attested affidavit. School verification and regular attendance mandatory. Only one girl child per family.
comparisons.scheme2_value: 30-day waiting period: natural death in first 30 days not covered (accidental death covered from day 1). Only ONE account allowed per person. Cover lapses if sufficient balance not maintained for auto-debit.

recommendation:
These are **two completely different schemes** serving different needs:

**Choose CBSE SGC Scholarship if:** You are a single girl child, aged 15–17, studying in CBSE class 11–12, scored 70%+ in class 10, attend a school with tuition ≤₹3,000/month, and your family income is ≤₹8 lakh/year. You need monthly educational financial support.

**Choose PMJJBY if:** You are aged 18–50 with a bank account and want affordable life insurance (death cover of ₹2 lakh) for your family. You can afford ₹436/year premium.

**You can do BOTH** if you qualify for both. They are not competing schemes — one funds education, the other protects your family financially.
